paper.title: Model Selection in Batch Policy Optimization

settings.name_in_paper: Batch linear contextual bandit with a single linear model class
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Batch/offline policy optimization from a fixed logged dataset (not an interactive bandit problem).
unmapped: Offline: learner is given a fixed dataset of n logged interactions (actions independent of potential outcomes given context) and outputs a policy
Known feature map phi(x,a); approximation error unknown
Regret against an arbitrary deterministic comparator policy, data-dependent coverage term E_X||phi(X,pi(X))||_{V^{-1}}
settings.definition_quote: the learner is given access to a fixed dataset $D = \{ x_i, a_i,y_i\}_{i \in [n]}$ of $n \in \N$ prior interactions ... We assume $f(x, a) \in [-1, 1]$ and the noise terms $\eta(a) = Y(a) - f(X, a)$ are independent across actions and sub-Gaussian with $\| \eta(a) \|_{\psi_2} \leq 1$.

settings.name_in_paper: Model selection in batch linear contextual bandit (arbitrary M linear model classes)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Batch/offline policy optimization and model selection from a fixed dataset.
unmapped: Offline fixed dataset of n interactions
M candidate linear model classes with known feature maps phi_k of dimension d_k; learner must compete with the best class
settings.definition_quote: We assume a collection of $M$ linear model classes $\FF_1, \ldots, \FF_M$, such that, for $k \in [M]$, $\FF_k = \left\{  (x, a) \mapsto \< \phi_k(x, a), \theta\> \ : \ \theta \in \R^{d_k} \right\}$ where $\phi_k$ is a known $d_k$-dimensional feature map

settings.name_in_paper: Model selection with nested linear model classes (lower bound)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Batch/offline policy optimization from a fixed dataset.
unmapped: Bound is a ratio against the oracle model-selection inequality
settings.definition_quote: The collection of linear model classes $\FF_1, \ldots, \FF_M$ with respective feature maps $\phi_1, \ldots, \phi_M$ is said to be nested if, for each map $\phi_{k +1}$, the first $d_k$ coordinates of $\phi_{k + 1}$ are the same as $\phi_k$

settings.name_in_paper: Model selection with data from a fixed behavior policy mu (approximation error-complexity trade-off)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Batch/offline policy optimization from a fixed dataset.
unmapped: Data sampled i.i.d. from D x mu for a fixed behavior policy mu; bounds depend on concentrability coefficient C(mu)
Centered sub-Gaussian features with positive definite covariance (Assumption 1); ||bar theta_k|| <= 1 (Assumption 2)
settings.definition_quote: We will now explicitly assume that the each $(x_i, a_i, y_i)$ in the dataset $D$ is sampled jointly from $\DD$ and a fixed behavior policy $\mu$

symbols.n_data: number of logged interactions in the batch dataset
symbols.eps_pi: approximation error epsilon(pi, hat pi) w.r.t. fixed-design least-squares parameter theta_*

conditions: holds for any deterministic comparator policy pi

source.label: thm::linear
source.quote: Let $\hat \pi$ be the output policy of Algorithm~\ref{alg::linear} with $\lambda > 0$. ... If $\| \theta_* \| \leq \sqrt{d}$, then with probability at least $1 - \delta$, for any policy $\pi$ (including the optimal policy), $\regret(\pi, \hat \pi)$ is bounded above by $\epsilon(\pi, \hat \pi) + 2\beta_{\lambda, \delta}(n, d) \cdot \E_X \| \phi(X, \pi(X)) \|_{V^{-1}}$

results.notes: Regret of a single output policy (simple-regret-like). Paper also states the O-tilde form eps + sqrt(d/n)*coverage.

symbols.oracle_k: min_k { eps_k(pi, hat pi) + sqrt(d_k/n) E_X ||phi_k(X,pi(X))||_{V_k^{-1}} }

conditions: for a particular nested collection of linear model classes
for any algorithm A there exists an instance, comparator and dataset
construction: two arms, single context, Gaussian unit-variance rewards, imbalanced dataset

source.label: thm::lower-bound
source.quote: Let $\FF_1, \ldots, \FF_M$ be a particular nested collection of linear model classes in the sense of Definition~\ref{def::nested}. For any $\alpha > 0$, there is $n = \Omega(\alpha^2)$ such that for any algorithm $A$ there is a contextual bandit instance with comparator $\pi$ and dataset $D$ with $n$ interactions consistent with $\DD$ that satisfies [ratio] \geq \alpha.

results.notes: Impossibility of oracle inequality; expectation over reward randomness in the dataset.

symbols.sum_eps_k: sum over the M classes of approximation errors eps_k(pi, hat pi)

conditions: holds for any comparator policy pi

source.label: thm::cov-est
source.quote: Given arbitrary linear model classes $\FF_1, \ldots, \FF_M$, Algorithm~\ref{alg::est-cov} outputs a policy $\hat \pi$ such that, with probability at least $1 - \delta$, for any comparator policy $\pi$, the regret $\regret(\pi, \hat \pi)$ is bounded above by $\min_{k \in [M]} \{ 2\beta_{\lambda, \delta/M}(n, d_k) \cdot \E_X \| \phi_k(X, \pi(X)) \|_{V_k^{-1}}\} + 2 \sum_{k \in [M]}\epsilon_{k}(\pi, \hat \pi)$

results.notes: Under realizability for all classes gives O(min_k sqrt(d_k log(M/delta)/n) * coverage_k). Norm precondition from Theorem 1 implicitly needed via Lemma 4.

symbols.oracle_ae: min_k { tilde eps_k + zeta_k(delta/M) * E_X max_a ||phi_k(X,a)||_{V_k^{-1}} }, tilde eps_k = min_theta 2 sqrt(C(mu) E_mu(<phi_k,theta> - f)^2), zeta_k ~ sqrt(d_k ||V_k^{-1}|| log(d_k M/delta)/n)

conditions: nested collection of linear model classes
Assumption 1: centered sub-Gaussian features with positive definite covariance
data drawn i.i.d. from D x mu for fixed behavior policy mu

source.label: thm::approx-est
source.quote: Let $\FF_1, \ldots, \FF_M$ be a nested collection of linear model classes. For $\lambda_k = 1$ for all $k \in [M]$, Algorithm~\ref{alg::approx-est} outputs a policy $\hat \pi$ such that, with probability at least $1 - 4\delta$, for any comparator policy $\pi$, $\regret(\pi, \hat \pi) \leq 12 \min_{k \in [M]} \{ \tilde \epsilon_k + \zeta_k(\delta/M) \cdot \E_X \max_a \| \phi_k(X, a) \|_{V_k^{-1}} \}$.

results.notes: Coverage term is worst-case over actions rather than comparator-specific.

symbols.oracle_ho: min_k { tilde eps_k + C sqrt(C(mu)) ||hat theta_k - bar theta_k||_{Sigma_k} }

conditions: data drawn i.i.d. from D x mu for fixed behavior policy mu
tuning: dataset split into D_in and D_out
